body:
PR #2026 (BUG-1441) — RequestChanges at 9c38af7d83, hold armed. The fix is right; one insertion inverts the code-to-decision linkage.

HOW I FOUND IT MATTERS FOR BUG-1549: #2026 is one of the SEVEN whose refusal was recorded by "aida drain reviewer", the exited actor. The shipped STORY-1419 row could not have told me — recorded_by does not match my seat, so it is filtered before the sha comparison even happens. My general sweep caught it, and the sweep's POPULATION COUNT is what made it visible: the open set dropped 15 to 14 when #2048 merged, which is the only reason I looked. That is the second time tonight the denominator did the work.

THE FIX IS GOOD AND I WANT THAT FIRST. The drain reviewer's finding was that the missing-current-member fallback lived only in render_human_inner. This resolves it at the SEAM rather than at the two cited sites: display_members is one view and all three renderers consume it — the human loop, render_toon_inner passing &display_members(state), and render_json_inner overriding the serde-emitted members key with the same view. The reasoning for NOT normalising at the loader is measured rather than asserted: six non-test read-mutate-write sites, five of which write the value back, so a synthetic inserted at load could reach disk and be read back as real state. There is a test pinning that the synthetic never persists. And one of the four mutations caught a WRONG ASSERTION — a bare contains() on the TOON document passed with the TOON fix reverted, because TOON emits current as a scalar too, so it now parses the members table. An assertion passing for the wrong reason also falsely reports coverage; catching that is exactly the self-falsification only the implementer can do.

THE BLOCKING FINDING. drain_state.rs:1429-1430 are "/// Render the human summary with project-local pacing context." and "// trace:STORY-948 | ai:codex" — the header for render_human_with_context. The new display_members was inserted BETWEEN that header and its function. So now:

    :1429-1430  STORY-948 header  ->  now sits above display_members
    :1450-1451  trace:BUG-1441 + fn display_members
    :1469       pub(crate) fn render_human_with_context  <- no doc, no trace

I VERIFIED THE CONSEQUENCE EMPIRICALLY RATHER THAN FROM CLAUDE.md: `aida why aida-cli-lib/src/drain_state.rs:1419` on current main returns "this code exists because of STORY-948", confirming it resolves the nearest PRECEDING trace comment. After this change, aida why on display_members resolves STORY-948 (wrong, it is BUG-1441) and aida why on render_human_with_context resolves BUG-1441 (wrong, it is STORY-948). Both inverted.

THIS IS WHY IT IS BLOCKING WHERE THE SAME SLIP WAS NOT. On #2047 the identical insertion displaced PROSE — short_sha_for_row took pluralize's description, and a test helper took a regression test's rationale. I graded that non-blocking, it shipped, and it needed BUG-1545. Here the displaced line is a TRACE comment, which is the substrate `aida why` reads. A misplaced prose line misinforms a reader; a misplaced trace line misinforms the query this project treats as its northstar. The escalation from prose to trace is the whole difference.

AND IT IS THE THIRD OCCURRENCE TONIGHT, second by this seat after it was raised. Three in one night is a habit, not an accident. I am not proposing a spec for it — that is yours — but if BUG-1545 is still open it may want the general form rather than the two awaiting_you.rs instances: an item inserted after a doc/trace header rather than before it, which the compiler never catches because both placements compile.

FIX IS TWO LINES EITHER WAY: move display_members below render_human_with_context, or move :1429-1430 down to sit immediately above :1469.
subject: #2026 BUG-1441: fix is right, but the insertion displaced a TRACE comment and inverts aida why for two functions — third instance of this slip tonight
